title: Software-Style Hardware Debugging: A Hardware Generation, Simulation and Debugging Framework
problem: Hardware verification still relies on traditional RTL workflows, creating a bottleneck in design-verification iteration efficiency and limiting the use of modern debugging techniques.
motivation: Hardware design iteration cycles are slow compared to software; bringing software debugging paradigms to hardware can significantly accelerate development.
method: ComoPy framework enables host language native simulation with fine-grained tracing and breakpoints on HDL source lines, software-style hot-reloading for incremental debug-fix cycles, and dynamic switching between fast low-level RTL simulation and high-level HDL execution.
key_novelty: Applying software debugging paradigms (breakpoints, tracing, hot-reloading) directly to hardware verification through host language integration.
contributions: Host language native simulation enabling breakpoints and tracing on HDL source lines
Software-style hot-reloading for incremental debug-fix iterations
Dynamic switching between RTL and HDL execution levels
limitations: Case studies limited to two examples (Sodor-clone processor and database accelerator); broader evaluation needed.
